summary: One focused, independently testable behavior: route every shake source through a single low-frequency-gated shake path in the camera/render layer that applies the section 16 amplitude budget (per-event and accumulated) and consults a master presentation flag (off = no shake from any source; the exact seam WI-06g's screen-shake toggle flips). Two changed responsibilities within one concrete owner (camera - low-frequency shake path): the gated emission path (low-frequency gate + amplitude budget) and the presentation flag; unit tests do not add responsibilities. Both scope checks hold: behavior_count 1, one declared subsystem, two named responsibilities (<=3); it is not splittable because a further split would leave each child with the same single parent criterion and could not form a strict subset of the one subsystem. AC-shake-rules is carried verbatim from WI-06d-c, and with sibling WI-06d-c-b retaining AC-widescreen the union covers both parent criteria; this leaf is the named final proof owner. The dependency is correct and acyclic: it inherits [WI-06a, WI-06b, WI-06c] from the parent and adds WI-06d-b4, whose distant-motion impulse is the concrete shake source for the browser proof (WI-06d-b4 depends only on WI-06a/b/c, is in a sibling story, and defers the flag->gate integration proof to WI-06d-c). Evidence is focused: Node unit tests for the flag plumbing, the low-frequency gate, and the amplitude budget, plus a browser final proof with the WI-06d-b4 impulse as the source (flag on = low-frequency shake within budget; flag off = no shake from any source). Boundaries and non-goals are explicit (no new shake sources, no settings UI, no widescreen work, no gameplay/balance/content changes) and the handoff names the owners, the WI-06g seam, and request section 16. Note: WI-06d-b4's AC text loosely says the impulse 'sets the presentation flag'; WI-06d-c-a defines that flag as the master on/off, and WI-06d-b4 already defers the flag->gate integration proof to this leaf, so this does not expand or contradict this node's boundaries.
